memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'When a man has sexual relations with a woman and there is an emission of semen, both of them must bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.'" - Lev 15:18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Both of them. Not the woman alone. Not the man alone. Together.

That word deserves attention. In the ancient world, laws about purity often fell far more heavily on women. Here God writes them side by side, with the same requirement and the same duration. Both bathe. Both wait. Both are restored at the same evening.

Scripture keeps doing this. Paul writes that the husband's body does not belong to him alone but also to his wife — and in the same breath, that the wife's body does not belong to her alone but also to her husband (1 Cor 7:4). Mutual. Reciprocal. Neither one holding power over the other.

Marriage in God's design is a shared life, not a hierarchy of value. Two people, equally made in His image, walking the same road, needing the same grace.

If you are married, there is something quietly practical in this. You are in it together — the washing, the waiting, the ordinary rhythms. Not one person keeping the rules while the other is served. Both, together, before God.

And if the marriage is under strain, that shared standing is worth remembering. You are not opponents. You are two people who need the same mercy.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. In your marriage or close relationships, is the burden genuinely shared?
2. Where have you expected more of someone than you expect of yourself?
3. What would "both together" look like in your home this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You deal with us equally and fairly. In my closest relationships, keep me from double standards, and make us people who walk together before You. Amen.
